title: High-resolution light microscopy imaging of polytene chromosomes
protocol: Grow D. melanogaster larvae at 18°C in fly bottles on standard fly food.
Use full grown, 3rd instar larvae for not more than two days from the start of their emergence.
Transfer several larvae to 35 mm Petri dishes with ~100 μl water.
Give heat-shock for transgene lac repressor expression if needed.
Place the Petri dish with larvae on ice for ~20 min to immobilize larvae.
Using fine-point forceps, dissect salivary glands in TB1 buffer on the glass slide with a 1.5 mm depression.
Remove head parts and most fat body.
Rinse glands with 20 μl Pipetman adjusted to 7-8 μl volume.
Transfer glands with the same Pipetman tip to fixative on another slide with a well depression.
Fix exactly 2 min.
While the glands are being fixed, attach a 22 mm square coverslip to the center of a glass slide with a small amount (3-4 μl) of water.
Dispose of the anterior pars of glands with the ducts.
Transfer not more than one pair of glands per preparation in exactly 7 μl of the fixative to the center of the coverslip.
Cover the preparation with an 18 mm square siliconized coverslip.
Cover the glass slide with a 25 mm wide strip of Whatman filter paper (0.2 mm thickness).
Tape a 40 mm wide piece of clear plastic film on top of the filter paper.
Use a Dremel Flex-Shaft attachment with a soft plastic tip having 6-12 smooth, protruding knobs around its circumference.
Cut 200 μl Pipetman plastic tips close to the wide base and create triangular notches around the end circumference.
Lightly melt the cut tip end on a gas burner to form rounded, slightly protruding (1.5 mm) knobs.
Rotate the Dremel Flex-Shaft attachment at 200 rpm and gently touch the preparation with the knobbed rotating tip positioned at ~45° to the surface.
Use spiral movements to spread chromosomes from the coverslip center towards its periphery.
Periodically remove the filter paper and film to monitor chromosome spreading under a phase contrast microscope.
Continue the process until chromosomes appear satisfactorily spread without much overlapping cell debris.
Start pressing the preparation lightly, gradually increasing pressure by sliding movements of the thumb over the area of the coverslip.
Firmly press with the thumb to finish removing excess fixative.
Remove filter paper and plastic film from the preparation.
Cover the preparation with a strip of silicone-impregnated paper (0.12 mm thickness) siliconized side facing the coverslip.
Place another glass slide on top of the covered preparation.
Align the layers carefully.
Place the glass slide sandwich in the center of an Avenger Gold toolmaker, tin coated, precision MTC-200-1 vise or a comparable model with high surface parallelism.
Use a torque wrench to tighten the vise.
Keep moving surfaces and tightening threads moderately oiled.
Press the preparation lightly up to 3 newton meters for 2 minutes.
Gradually increase pressure up to 17 newton meters, maintaining it for about 1 minute.
Release the vise pressure gradually.
Transfer the slide with coverslips to liquid nitrogen for less than 1 minute.
Flip the top siliconized coverslip off with a razor blade.
Place the slide with remaining coverslip into 100% EtOH to thaw for 20 seconds before removal of the coverslip from the glass slide.
Store coverslips within sealed 35 mm Petri dishes in 100% EtOH at -20°C for up to one week.
Proceed with FISH or immunostaining if planned.
Use DAPI, 20 ng/ml in PBS or other buffers, for DNA staining for 15-30 minutes.
Use fluorescence microscope to acquire one best focused optical section of the areas of interest.
Use Photoshop to minimally process the image by changing brightness and contrast.
Apply "unsharp mask" filter in Photoshop to improve print quality.
